shortened: These are among the most exalted of creatures in the Tablet of imperishable glory. They are servants who call all who are on earth behind them and turn toward the countenance of God with pure and illumined hearts.

order.why: Follow hearing and arrival into assistance.
shortened: Blessed is he who has drawn nigh unto Him, and has attained unto His days, and has heard His verses, and has arisen to serve and assist Him. He is of those whom God has made sanctified from all that has been created in the realm of creation."

order.why: Consider remembrance and service as things that endure.
Read assistance as an opportunity offered to souls.
shortened: Though by God's grace it hath been and shall ever be raised aloft, and the Truth hath by its own essence aided and shall ever aid His Cause, yet the purpose is that souls who are reckoned among the Concourse on High may attain unto the most great honor and be deprived of no bounty whatsoever.

order.why: Test wealth through charitable use.
shortened: Thus it became clear that the end of the wealthy is regret upon regret, except for the rich person who pours forth treasure from his sleeve for charitable causes and expends his wealth in benevolent matters. Such blessed souls shine like brilliant stars from the horizon of eternal glory.

order.why: Keep spiritual hope beside debts, family and practical responsibilities.
Let generosity prefer others even in poverty.
Receive the concise description of the faithful path.
shortened: This beseemeth the believers; this is the qualification of the sincere; this is the path of the knowers, and this is the utmost aim of the faithful.

order.why: Keep the affectionate image of sweetness as encouragement.
shortened: If you wish for my heart's delight, raise this melody. I swear by your precious life that the reward will be very rich and sweet, delicious and savory, like the musk candy of Rasht and the baklava of Qazvin.

order.why: Let every breath become gratitude.
shortened: Therefore, with every breath you must render a hundred thousand thanksgivings at the Threshold of the One God, for you have been blessed with the bounty of guidance, have entered the circle of the lovers, and are counted among the company of the yearning ones.

order.why: Retain the supplied explanation of why the full station remains concealed.
Keep the supplied comparison with prophets and its stated qualification.
End with living the teachings visibly through love and harmony.
shortened: The great thing is to 'Live the Life' -- to have our lives so saturated with the Divine teaching and the Baha'i Spirit that people cannot fail to see a joy, a power, a love, a purity, a radiance, an efficiency in our character and work that will distinguish us from worldly-minded people and make people wonder what is the secret of this new life in us.
Unless we can show this transformation in our lives, this new power, this mutual love and harmony, then the Baha'i teachings are but a name to us.

questions: How do the passages’ images of hidden worth challenge familiar ways of judging oneself and other people?
What relationship do these readings establish between spiritual distinction, grace, humility, and service?
How do the many addresses to women reshape the meaning of dignity, sovereignty, and lasting influence?
What do the repeated calls to preserve a station suggest about the relationship between receiving a gift and living responsibly?
How do Mark’s account of greatness and First Peter’s account of a chosen people help us examine the responsibilities and possible misunderstandings of religious distinction?
What would make a community’s professed calling recognizable through its treatment of others, especially amid hardship, inequality, and differences of belief?

references.label: 1 · Mark 10:35–45 · Greatness through serving
references.note: James and John request places of honor, and the conversation turns toward suffering, authority, and service. Jesus makes serving others the measure of greatness and connects it with his own mission. Compare this reversal with the compilation’s crowns and sovereignty of servitude, preserving the Gospel’s particular account of the Son of man.

references.label: 2 · 1 Peter 2:9–12 · A chosen people and visible conduct
references.note: The letter addresses a community through images of election, royalty, mercy, and light, then asks for conduct whose good works others can observe. Read these verses beside the compilation’s assurances of dignity and demands for trustworthy character. Consider how belonging to a religious community becomes a responsibility toward people beyond it.
